editionLabel: English CGE base-game rules, 20-page publisher booklet
location: Starting Player Token; Choosing Play Order and Declaring Actions
firstPlayerRule: Whoever was most recently in a laboratory receives the starting-player token and chooses an order space first.
clarifications: The other players choose order spaces clockwise. Those spaces determine play order for the rest of the round; the token holder is not necessarily first to perform an action.
Players declare actions from the lowest order space upward, then resolve actions from the highest space downward.

location: Setup; The Round and The Narrator
firstPlayerRule: The person who looks most like a moose is the first narrator. The rules also allow the group to choose the narrator however it likes.
officialTieBreak: Among tied players, choose whoever looks most like a rabbit. If a tie remains, choose randomly.
clarifications: The narrator reads and reveals cards to lead the round; the other players react together. This selects a role, rather than the first ordinary turn.

editionLabel: English CGE base-game rules, 24-page publisher booklet
location: First Game setup, Starting Player Token; Selecting and Revealing Orders
firstPlayerRule: Give the starting-player token to the nicest player, or choose its holder randomly.
officialTieBreak: Random selection is an explicit alternative in the rulebook; it is not restricted to ties.
clarifications: Players select orders simultaneously. After the first orders are revealed, the token holder places a minion first, followed by the others clockwise.

location: Starting Player Token; Going Shopping, Biggest Group Goes First
firstPlayerRule: Whoever fed a pet most recently receives the starting-player token. The rules also permit choosing its holder randomly or by agreement.
officialTieBreak: For shopping groups of equal size, resolve them clockwise beginning with the starting-player token holder. Choosing that token holder randomly is also an official setup alternative.
clarifications: The token does not guarantee the first shopping action. After players reveal their groups, the largest group goes first; its size counts both imps and gold tokens.

location: Build! Starting Player and Swapping Jobs; three-player Team Rules
firstPlayerRule: In the standard four-player game, whoever opened the box is the first round's starting player. That player and the opponent opposite them plan first.
officialTieBreak: In the three-player variant, the lower-scoring member of the two-person team starts alongside the solo player; roll a die if those teammates are tied. The die also breaks lowest-score ties when selecting a starter for later rounds.
clarifications: During the four-player build, two players plan while their partners wait to build, then the roles switch. There is not a single player taking the whole opening turn alone.
The box-opening instruction applies to the first round. Later rounds use the lowest score.
uncertainty: No tie-break is stated specifically for the opening box-opener criterion.

location: Player setup; Planning and Planning in a 2-player game
firstPlayerRule: Whoever most recently paid for something receives the starting-player marker and begins the planning phase.
clarifications: With three or more players, the marker holder chooses a plan first, followed clockwise by the others. The chosen plans determine order for the remaining phases.
With two players, the marker holder first blocks a plan with a neutral marker. The opponent blocks another and chooses their own plan; the marker holder then chooses from the remaining plans.

location: Player Setup, Play Order; Solo Variant, Gameplay
firstPlayerRule: Whoever most recently traveled somewhere they had never visited before takes the starting-player marker and starts.
clarifications: Multiplayer turns proceed clockwise. In the solo variant, the automated rival starts each of the five rounds.

firstPlayerRule: Whoever saw a UFO most recently takes the starting-player marker and starts.
clarifications: Multiplayer turns proceed clockwise. Starting scores are one, two, three and four points in turn order.

location: Setting Up the Game, Starting Player
firstPlayerRule: The player who most recently sacrificed something receives the starting-player marker.
officialTieBreak: If tied, give the marker to the player who volunteers for the next sacrifice.
uncertainty: This thematic setup instruction does not define what counts as a sacrifice.
